title:
Two Directors, One Oscar: Can Lord and Miller, Los Javis, Fielder and
 Oppenheim or the Esiri Brothers Break Through?
summary: Co-directing teams gain Oscar momentum, reflecting growing acceptance of shared directing credits and opportunities for partnerships.
content: Awards Circuit Column: The Academy’s Directors Branch has given best director to a duo only three times in 98 years. This season, four teams are vying for attention Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi, Phil Lord and Chris Miller and Nigeria’s Esiri brothers are chasing a prize the Academy’s Director Branch has handed to a duo only three times in its history. Looking at the two-name directing teams in this year’s Oscar race, artistic collaboration seems to be having a moment. Not everyone sees it that way. Related Stories ‘Once Upon a Time in Harlem’ Duo Praise Neon’s Strategy to Reach Young Audiences How Soviet TV Audiences Fell Under the Spell of Mass Hypnosis Artist Anatoly Kashpirovskiy “If you need two of you to make the film, then I think that’s a problem,” one prominent member of the Directors Branch bluntly tells Variety. Fielder and Oppenheim turned Elizabeth Holmes’ saga into the slippery A24 documentary “ You Can See Everything .” Calvo and Ambrossi, the Spanish duo known as Los Javis, are carrying their country’s international feature hopes with “ La Bola Negra .” Lord and Miller reunited behind the camera for Amazon MGM’s sci-fi swing “Project Hail Mary.” And twin brothers Arie and Chuko Esiri helmed Neon’s ambitious “Clarissa,” a reimagining of “Mrs. Dalloway.” All four teams face a stubborn piece of Academy history: The Directors Branch does not like splitting statuettes. In 98 years, only four directing duos have received best director nominations (one of them twice). This year, several are within earshot of nods. Robert Wise and Jerome Robbins got there first for 1961’s “West Side Story.” Their partnership was so combustible that Robbins was fired mid-production for running over schedule and budget. He retained his credit and collected the Oscar. Warren Beatty and Buck Henry followed with “Heaven Can Wait” (1978), but lost to Michael Cimino (“The Deer Hunter”). title: Teyana Taylor Sells Female-Driven Comedy to Warner Bros. (Exclusive)
summary: Teyana Taylor sets a female-led comedy at Warner Bros., co-writing, producing, and likely directing—opening casting and staffing prospects.
content: Teyana Taylor is plotting her next moves as a filmmaker. The Oscar-nominated actress has sold an original comedy pitch to Warner Bros . that she will co-write and produce via her The Aunties banner alongside producing partner Coco Gilbert. Taylor would also likely direct the project, described as a female-driven, wish fulfillment comedy that explores the chaos of modern dating, and which draws upon stories Taylor has logged from friends, family, homegirl group chats, and her own experiences. The project is in early development at Warners and specific plot details are being kept under wraps. Related Stories Movies 'You've Got Mail' Reboot in the Works at Warner Bros. Business Pam Abdy Laments Exits of Top Female Executives in Hollywood: "It Is Upsetting to See" Taylor earned an Oscar nomination earlier this year for One Battle After Another , which won multiple Oscars, including best picture as well as best director and best adapted screenplay for filmmaker Paul Thomas Anderson. The role of revolutionary Perfidia Beverly Hills also earned Taylor a Golden Globe and a BET Award. The Grammy nominee came up in the world of music, and had already amassed a number of acting credits, but the film and its accolades put her acting career on a whole new trajectory. Since then, she’s been focused on her directorial debut, the Paramount feature Get Lite . The film is in post-production as it heads toward an Aug. 20 2027 release date. It stars Storm Reid and per the logline, centers on “a talented, but sheltered, dance student” who “finds inspiration, love, and family in the last place he expected: the subways of New York City.” It also stars NFL prospect Ceyair Wright.

title: 'Gilded Age' Scores Early Season 5 Renewal at HBO
summary: HBO renews The Gilded Age for Season 5, ensuring continued roles and hiring for period-drama actors and crew.
content: The news comes after the period drama has aired just three of its eight episodes for Season 4. This marks the earliest renewal announcement for the show to date, which has continued to grow its audience season to season. Per HBO, Season 4 is averaging 5.9 million U.S. multiplatform viewers per episode to date, with episode three hitting 4.3 million viewers in three days time. The episodic average is up nearly 20% over Season 3, though there are still five more episodes to air. title: Brooks Nader Joins ‘Playmates’ Movie at Searchlight (EXCLUSIVE)
summary: Searchlight’s Playmates adds Brooks Nader to its cast, signaling active production and further casting opportunities.
content: Brooks Nader is the latest addition to the cast of the upcoming Searchlight movie “ Playmates ,” Variety has learned exclusively. The film is inspired by writer and director Lorraine Nicholson’s childhood experiences at the Playboy Mansion. Nader will appear alongside previously announced cast members Lily-Rose Depp, Bill Pullman, Jessica Biel, Indiana Elle, and Anna Van Patten. She originally found success as a model, including appearing in the iconic Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue. She also currently stars in the Freeform reality series “Love Thy Nader,” which is prepping a second season, and also appeared in the 33rd season of “Dancing with the Stars.” She is repped by WME, Dixon Talent, Inc. and by Leigh Fidler, Chief Brand Officer of Nader Sisters Inc. title: ‘GTA 6’ Hits Massive $3.79 Billion in First-Day Sales
summary: GTA 6’s record-shattering launch underscores booming game budgets and rising demand for voice and performance-capture talent.
content: Crime pays: Rockstar Games’ “ Grand Theft Auto 6″ preorder and first-day sales reached $3.79 billion, the game developer announced Friday. Per Rockstar Games parent company Take-Two Interactive, that total sets “a new record for entertainment across any medium” and makes “ GTA 6 ” “the biggest entertainment launch in history.” A spokesperson for Take-Two Interactive declined to comment on the number of “GTA 6” copies sold. Related Stories Berlin Winner Tatiana Huezo Close to Completing Road Movie ‘Galerna’ Following Awards Boost: ‘I’m Dying to Finish It’ ‘White Tiger Column’ Directors on How Myanmar’s Resistance Speaks to Political Youth Movements in Brazil, Serbia and the U.S.: ‘Revolution Is on the Lips of a Lot of People’ For the sake of comparison, Sony Pictures’ “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” reaped $2.52 billion at the global box office in 2026, the No. 1 movie of the year to date. Christopher Nolan’s blockbuster “The Odyssey” has taken in just over $1.8 billion to date. On its first day of release, “GTA 6” made roughly as much as James Cameron’s last two “Avatar” movies, “The Way of Water” and “Fire and Ash,” have grossed combined. With just Day 1 sales, “GTA 6” has already out-grossed the highest grossing movie of all time, “Avengers: Endgame” ($2.9 billion), in one day. The game cost a reported $1.5 billion to produce over more than a decade of development. “GTA 6” launched Thursday for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X and S and was also available on Xbox One via Xbox’s Cloud Gaming service. The game retails at $80 for the standard edition and $100 for the ultimate version. Preorders for “GTA 6” opened June 25. With a reported total gameplay time of approximately 80 hours to complete its main storyline, “GTA 6” follows duo Jason and Lucia as they navigate their way through criminal life in the fictional Leonida. “GTA 6” has reached a 99 Metacritic score (tying it for the highest-rated video game of all time) and received a nomination for Game of the Year at The Ga

title: ‘Disclosure Day’ Did Its Biggest Stunts Practically, So the VFX Team Worked Hard to Look Invisible — Watch
summary: Disclosure Day favored practical stunts with seamless VFX, underscoring collaboration and planning actors need for action-heavy shoots.
content: Even six decades into his Hollywood career, Steven Spielberg is still synonymous with a brand of movie magic and spectacle that very few can rival. And when he decides to direct a new popcorn blockbuster like “ Disclosure Day ,” you know you’re in for a few dazzling sequences. One of the most exciting moments in the film comes when a train collides into a car with stars Josh O’Connor and Emily Blunt close at hand. The sequence tested every department, from camera and production design to visual effects. And during IndieWire’s recent Craft Roundtables, VFX Supervisor Matthew Butler explained the unique challenge of incorporating subtle VFX work into a scene where so much happens in camera. Related Stories How World-Class Filmmaker Andrey Zvyagintsev Came Back to Life for ‘Minotaur’ How a Filipino Facial Expression in ‘Forgotten Island’ Became a Universal Symbol of Representation “With Steven, he wants everything to be as practical as it can be,” Butler said. “We had a real train. A real train, a real car attached to that train, it was being dragged on a real track. That actually did happen.” But while Spielberg’s preferences were clear, Butler clarified that blockbusters on this scale rarely come down to a binary choice between practical effects and VFX. The biggest scenes often contain elements of both, as the pairing between in-camera human acting and cutting edge post-production is what leads to movie magic. “When you combine some of the live action blue screen work, clearly that’s your lead actor and actress there, and your stunt work where it’s like ‘Oh my God, that looks really real’ and the stuff that you just can’t do that’s just too dangerous … that’s where visual effects came in,” he said. “But I wouldn’t say it was a visual effects sequence. It was a sequence that contained all of those, and it came together in the right way.” More coverage from IndieWire’s Craft Roundtables will be published here over the coming weeks. title: Robert Pattinson’s Bond Ascent: How Pricey Screen Tests and Amazon Execs Landed a Starry 007
summary: High-cost screen tests and Amazon leadership shaped Bond casting, signaling streamer-led franchise decisions and rigorous audition stakes.
content: What does an actor do in the quiet moments before the announcement that will change his life? For Robert Pattinson , there were about 12 hours between the Sunday phone call confirming he’d landed the role of James Bond and Amazon MGM’s Monday-morning release of the first image of the actor rocking a tuxedo and pistol. He spent it, rather predictably, watching an arthouse horror film. Related Stories Laura Poitras Turns Lens on ICE's 'Paramilitary Occupation' of Minneapolis in 'They’re Here' Berlin Winner Tatiana Huezo Close to Completing Road Movie ‘Galerna’ Following Awards Boost: ‘I’m Dying to Finish It’ His longtime friend and collaborator Robert Eggers told Variety this week that Pattinson was screening the director’s forthcoming genre drama “Werwulf” when the Bond news broke. Nothing like a stark naked Aaron Taylor-Johnson terrorizing a quaint village to pass the time. But after months (years, really) of toiling and speculation over who would replace Daniel Craig in the film adaptations of Ian Fleming’s spy novels, Pattinson took the crown. It buttons up a delicious, messy and very public guessing game over which lucky man would land the iconic role. When Amazon MGM bought out rights to James Bond from longtime custodians the Broccoli family in 2025, intentions were set for a young star who could shoulder the franchise for a decade or two. An A-list team of producers (Amy Pascal of “Spider-Man” and David Heyman of the “Harry Potter” movies) recruited Denis Villeneuve to direct. Together, with significant influence from Amazon execs Courtenay Valenti and Mike Hopkins (and yes, Jeff Bezos), they screen-tested a laundry list of virile performers — including Callum Turner, Tom Francis, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor — earlier this year. For the curious, the batch of screen tests cost Amazon MGM between $300,000 and $500,000 to pull off, ostensibly in secret (everyone found out), sources familiar with the process say. title: E. Lockhart, Gotham Group Tackling Fantasy Novel ‘The Curse Workers’ for 20th Television (Exclusive)
summary: 20th Television developing Holly Black’s Curse Workers trilogy with E. Lockhart and Gotham Group, creating fantasy series casting opportunities.
content: 20 th Television is in development on The Curse Workers , the best-selling fantasy books from Holly Black , with a plan to adapt it for a TV series to stream on Disney+. E. Lockhart, the author turned showrunner behind Prime Video’s hit We Were Liars , will adapt the trilogy into a series, serving as writer and executive producer. Also exec producing are Ellen Goldsmith-Vein and Jeremy Bell for The Gotham Group. The project marks a reunion for Gotham Group and Black; the company produced the 2023 series adaptation of The Spiderwick Chronicles , based on the children’s series that Black co-wrote with Tony DiTerlizzi. Related Stories TV War Is Coming in the 'Percy Jackson' Season 3 Trailer TV Series Based on Rick Riordan's 'Kane Chronicles' in the Works at Disney+ Curse Workers is set in a world where magic is illegal and controlled by the Mob. The story centers on Cassel Sharpe, the youngest son of a criminal family and the only one without magic. When his mother returns from prison, his brothers start acting strange, and his own memories are no longer making sense, forcing him to rely on his knowledge of con artistry to uncover the truth. Lockhart is the New York Times bestselling author who wrote the book sensation We Were Liars , and then was intimately involved in the book’s translation to mystery thriller series, which reached No. 1 on Prime Video and was quickly renewed for a second season, now in production. Lockhart wrote the season one finale, participated in casting and location scouting, and continues as an executive producer on season two, which incorporates the story of her prequel novel, Family of Liars . In addition to Liars , Lockhart is adapting her own novel Again Again for Wayfarer Entertainment while novel Genuine Fraud is in development as a series at Prime Video, with Rain Spencer attached to star and Sinead Daly writing the pilot. title: Curry Barker Would Have Completely Reshot 'Obsession' If He Could
summary: Curry Barker regrets Obsession, saying he'd reshoot entirely, underscoring the importance of time and control for quality.
content: It’s been quite a year for Curry Barker . In September 2025, he brought his $700,000 horror film to the Toronto International Film Festival, where it sparked a bidding war that Focus Features won for $17 million. That hefty price tag turned into the deal of the century, as “ Obsession ” went on to become a half-billion-dollar box-office sensation, with audiences growing week to week . It was clear the then 26-year-old “YouTuber” (a moniker Barker rightfully dismisses) was something special. This was not just a flash in the pan, but a real talent with a seemingly boundless number of ideas and movies he wanted to make. His next film, “Anything but Ghosts,” was already in the can by the “ Obsession ” premiere, a yet-to-be-announced third film is in the works, while potential franchises (“ Texas Chainsaw Massacre ” and “Obsession,” Barker sees the One Wish Willow story device having “Knives Out” anthology-like potential) linger in the background. Related Stories Director Brian Duffield Had to Find a New Form of Visual Storytelling for ‘Whalefall’ How ‘Paper Tiger’ Evolved When Jeremy Strong and Anne Hathaway Couldn’t Reprise Their ‘Armageddon Time’ Roles Which is why it’s interesting that Hollywood’s hottest new director took time out from editing (he’s cutting “Ghosts” himself) and writing (“I have my next thing that I’m working on — I’m really excited about it, and nobody knows anything about it, which is super exciting”), and an unexpected Oscar campaign (“Obsession” is a legit contender for Best Picture, Actress, and Original Screenplay nominations ), to make a 5-minute short film, “ Mama Bear .” On this week’s episode of the Filmmaker Toolkit Podcast , Barker talked about how the success of “Obsession” interrupted his established flow of churning out short-form content for his popular YouTube channel. “I have two or three short films where I’m like, ‘Oh man, this all took off really quickly, and I have this short film idea I’ve been dying to do,” said Barker on Too

title: Lili Reinhart in Talks to Join ‘Polly Pocket’ Movie After Lily Collins Exit
summary: Lili Reinhart negotiating to lead Polly Pocket film after Lily Collins exits, signaling a prime studio role opening.
content: Lili Reinhart is in discussions to star in and executive produce Amazon MGM and Mattel Studios’ “ Polly Pocket .” Reinhart joins the film after Lily Collins exited due to scheduling issues. Collins remains on as an executive producer. Clea DuVall will direct “Polly Pocket” with a screenplay from Dan Brier and Jordan Weiss. Producers include Robbie Brenner for Mattel Studios and Reese Witherspoon and Lauren Neustadter for Hello Sunshine. Mattel Studios, Hello Sunshine’s Emily Ferenbach, Jeff Waxman and Jennifer Madeloff serve as executive producers. “Polly Pocket” is set for release on Prime Video. Related Stories 'The Year of the Ghost,' About Misogyny in China, Wins Best Film at IDFA Documentary Festival 'NAZA' Filmmakers Grateful for 'Light Being Shone' on Their Film Through Awards Conversation but Prioritize Impact: It's a 'Small Cog in a Machine of Resistance’ Reinhart, best known for her role as Betty Cooper in CW’s teen soap “Riverdale,” recently starred in the Prime Video rom-com “The Love Hypothesis.” Reinhart’s other recent big-screen credits include “Forbidden Fruits,” “American Sweatshop” and “Look Both Ways.” Ever since Mattel hit big with 2023’s “Barbie,” the toy maker has pushed hard into the film market. 2026 saw the release of “Masters of the Universe,” which hit theaters in June, and “Matchbox,” which debuted on Apple TV in October. Other upcoming projects based on Mattel properties include “Barney” with Ayo Edebiri, “Hot Wheels” from producer J.J. Abrams and director Jon M. Chu and “Rock ‘Em Sock ‘Em Robots” written by and starring Vin Diesel. The Polly Pocket and her miniature play sets first hit shelves in the summer of 1989 through Bluebird Toys. Mattel acquired the brand in 1998. Mattel reintroduced the toy in 2018 with a more modern design to appeal to a new generation of kids.

title: Sterling K. Brown Eyed To Star Opposite Nicolas Cage In New ‘Longlegs’ Pic At Par
summary: Sterling K. Brown circling co-lead opposite Nicolas Cage in a new Longlegs project at Paramount.
content: EXCLUSIVE: Following the excitement that fans of the record-breaking hit Longlegs would be getting a new movie in the universe, Paramount Pictures looks to have now found the actor to lead that film as sources tell Deadline Sterling K. Brown is in negotiations to join Paramount Pictures’ upcoming Longlegs film. Brown will be joining Nicolas Cage who will be reprising his iconic role for the titular character. Osgood Perkins is back to direct and is also writing and will produce. Cage is also producing along with Brian Kavanaugh Jones through Range Media Partners, Perkins and Chris Ferguson, through their company Phobos; and Dave Caplan under his C2 banner, which originated the rights to the property. The pic will bow on January 14, 2028. Related Stories Casting Chris Pratt To Star In Paramount's Feature Take Of Joseph Eckert Novel 'The Traveler' News 'Longlegs' Producer Dan Kagan And His Banner Traffic Ink Partnership With Plan B When news broke that Perkins and Cage were returning for a new movie this past spring, people were floored that a new movie was not only in the works but was moving over to Paramount after originally being released by Neon. Watch on Deadline The original 2024 pic starred Cage and Maika Monroe as an FBI agent who investigates a series of murder-suicides in Oregon that are connected to serial killer nicknamed Longlegs. The film turned into one of Neon’s biggest hits to date grossing $128 million worldwide and also gave us another out of this world performance from Cage who earned some of the best reviews in recent years. Not much is known about this latest film or who Brown will be playing, but it is not a straight sequel and Monroe is not expected to return for this film. As for Brown, the three-time Emmy-winning actor and Oscar nominee continues to stay busy on both TV and film fronts. The third season of his Hulu series Paradise bows next year. title: Bruce Greenwood, Johnny Knoxville & Dylan Hawco Join ‘Fake Skating’ Adaptation At Sony
summary: Sony's Fake Skating adaptation adds Bruce Greenwood, Johnny Knoxville, and Dylan Hawco, indicating active casting on a studio comedy.
content: EXCLUSIVE: Bruce Greenwood , Johnny Knoxville and Dylan Hawco are set to round out the cast in Sony Pictures and Will Gluck’s Olive Bridge Entertainment’s Fake Skating based on Lynn Painter’s New York Times best-selling book with Amélie Hoeferle and Graham Campbell set to star. Josh Boone is directing from a screenplay written by Morgan Lehmann and Victoria Bata with revisions by Boone and his writing partner Knate Lee. This is the first book from the best-selling author to be adapted for the screen. Set for a summer release next year, Fake Skating is an emotional high school hockey romance about childhood sweethearts whose icy reunion in their hockey-loving hometown unexpectedly thaws when they fake a romantic relationship. Related Stories Casting 'Return Of The Living Dead' Sequel Gearing Up With Johnny Knoxville Among Cast Books Everything We Know About The 'Fake Skating' Film Adaptation So Far Winner of the 2025 Goodreads Choice Award for Young Adult Fiction, Fake Skating has nearly 500,000 copies in print and has appeared on the New York Times YA Hardcover Bestseller list 48 times since its release in September 2025, holding the #1 spot for 15 of those weeks. The novel has also been translated into 16 languages. Watch on Deadline Painter is the #1 New York Times and internationally best-selling author of Better Than the Movies, The Do-Over, Betting on You, Maid For Each Other, First and Forever, Nothing Like the Movies, and Fake Skating . Greenwood is best known for his roles in the film Thirteen Days where he portrayed President John F. Kennedy. Other notable film credits include I, Robot , Double Jeopardy , Capote , Star Trek and Star Trek Into Darkness, and The Post . His television credits include The Resident and the miniseries The Fall of the House of Usher. He is repped by Gersh and Binder & Associates. Knoxville can recently be seen in I Want Your Sex, Tiny Fugitives, and as the host of Fear Factor: House of Fear . He is repped by CAA and Sloane Offer.

title: ‘Godavari’ Director Nikhil Mahajan Turns a Malegaon Carjacking Into Neo-Noir With WAVES Film Bazaar Project ‘Mongoose’
summary: Nikhil Mahajan developing neo-noir Mongoose through Film Bazaar's WAVES program, creating upcoming casting and festival-market opportunities.
content: Nikhil Mahajan, the Indian National Film Award-winning director of “Godavari” and the Netflix series “Betaal,” is bringing “Mongoose,” a Marathi-language neo-noir thriller about a cab driver and the con man who steals his taxi, to the Co-Production Market at WAVES Film Bazaar . Set in the hardscrabble town of Malegaon, the film follows Abhimanyu, a hardworking driver whose hopes of owning his own taxi are wrecked when he is carjacked on the highway. The thief, Shahrukh, is a debt-ridden hustler who crashes the stolen cab, killing pilgrims traveling in a van, and the two men’s lives become violently entangled. As Abhimanyu chases justice and Shahrukh tries to stay free, it emerges that Abhimanyu’s own boss ordered the hit. Related Stories 'Hinotama: Ball of Fire' Review: Gentle, Handsomely Shot Domestic Drama Is a Promising Debut for Yaza Takenoshin Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Heist Drama '12 12 12' Feels Like a Bad Video Game: TV Review Mahajan says that, particularly since “Raavsaaheb,” he has been drawn to subjects that let him examine Indian society through a social lens, and that “Mongoose” digs into the gap between ambition and reality for one section of the population. “I choose to lend my genre sensibility to these social subjects to create a more wide appealing introspection of the Indian living condition.” Suhrud Godbole and Mahajan’s Coquelicot Pictures is producing with Sydney-based Photoplay Films. The budget is $1.1 million, with $650,000 in place. The project is in advanced development and the team aims to start prep in the second quarter of 2027. In Goa, they are looking for co-producers, sales agents and “early-stage festival programmers.” “At Coquelicot Pictures we are very driven and passionate about creating and supporting modern and cutting-edge storytelling. ‘Mongoose’ is a story we believe will cut across languages and demographics, and Nikhil is one of the finest genre-makers we have in the country today,” says Godbole, who has worked wi

title: Rich Eisen’s ‘Beautiful Day’: Landing All Four Members of U2 as Guests
summary: Rich Eisen's show booked all four U2 members, underscoring talk shows' demand for star power and cross-promotional appearances.
content: Rich Eisen came out on to the set of his long-running talk show the other day, only to find Bono from U2 doing an impression of the running-man logo that has long been a part of the program’s identifying marks. When Eisen went to take part, he discovered the person taking pictures of the encounter wasn’t the program’s staff photographer, but rather The Edge. Eisen calls it being “stuck in a moment I didn’t want to get out of.” And that’s the last U2 song joke we’ll make here. Related Stories Cannes Condemns Five-Year Prison Sentence Against Iranian Palme d’Or Winner Jafar Panahi and Pleads for International Support The host has long been known for his sportscasting and “The Rich Eisen Show” has long been featured as part of sports programming, but that doesn’t mean the host and the program can’t take a detour once in a while. “This is what our show is about. It’s a pop culture show,” Eisen says during a recent interview. “Sports is just one spoke on the pop culture wheel.” U2 holds forth with Eisen on Friday’s program. Eisen has over the years talked with Jon Bon Jovi, Jodie Foster, James Taylor, Will Ferrell, Kenny Chesney and Snoop Dogg, and there are reasons for him to do so. Since returning to the ESPN empire (Eisen was an ESPN regular between 1996 and 2003), Eisen’s show now streams on Disney+ and the ESPN App, among other venues. “We are exposed to a much larger audience of movies, television, music and sports fans,” says Eisen, adding: We put the word out 12 years ago that, yes, we are on sports talk radio, and yues, I’m known certain in my other jobs as a sportscaster, but I’m just as into movies and music and TV shows and live theater as anybody else.” How did Eisen’s team land U2? The band, which just released its first full album, Carnaval de Luz, in nine years, is scheduled to play the halftime show of Netflix’s stream of a Thanksgiving Eve game taking place between the Green Day Packers and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium. title:
A 'Home Alone' Legacyquel with Macaulay Culkin in Early Development
 with Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg
summary: A Home Alone legacy sequel with Macaulay Culkin is developing under Rogen and Goldberg, signaling upcoming comedy franchise casting.
content: The legacy-quel is alive and well , and it only makes sense that a sequel/reboot/reimagining would eventually come for “ Home Alone ,” Chris Columbus’ 1990 holiday classic starring Macaulay Culkin . There was buzz that Culkin over the summer pitched an idea to Disney as to where a grown Kevin McAllister would be today after enduring two child abandonments and harassment and attempted murder from bumbling bandits (our interpretation, not necessarily his read on Kevin’s childhood shenanigans and trauma). Disney now seems to have warmed to the idea like a cup of hot cocoa, especially thanks to the two additional names who are working with Culkin on the project: Seth Rogen and Evan Goldberg. Related Stories What ‘Digger’ Has in Common with Gary Oldman’s Winston Churchill and Charlize Theron’s Megyn Kelly ‘Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall’ Review: PTA’s Spellbinding Concert Doc Is a Gorgeously Tender Performance Disney’s 20th Century Studios is in early development on a sequel to “Home Alone” that would star Culkin reprising his original role and in which Rogen and Goldberg on behalf of their Point Grey banner would write and produce the film , working with Culkin on his idea, IndieWire has learned. Things are very, very early days, and any plot details are being kept under wraps for now, and no director is attached at the moment. Chris Columbus directed the original “Home Alone” and its nearly-as-loved sequel “Home Alone 2: Lost in New York,” and both written by the late great John Hughes. If you can believe it, there have been six “Home Alone” movies in all, with the third one at least released in theaters and doing respectable box office numbers. The others are all TV movies or in the case of the most recent 2021 film “Home Sweet Home Alone,” a Disney+ streaming movie. The original two films though grossed $477 million and $358 million worldwide, respectively, and the original still gets tons of cable play and finds its way into the Nielsen streaming charts. summary: Bowen Yang apologized for using an antisemitic term, underscoring reputational risks and language awareness for public-facing performers.
content: Bowen Yang has apologized after he received backlash recently for calling singer Regina Spektor an antisemitic slur on a past episode of his podcast, “Las Culturistas.” A resurfaced clip from his Oct. 14 podcast came under fire when Yang referred to Spektor as “Zio.” “I want to genuinely apologize for using a word on the podcast without knowing its antisemitic history, especially since we’ve repudiated antisemitism on the show as recently as the last two weeks,” Yang wrote on Instagram on Friday (his handle is @fayedunaway but has no connection to the actress). “Particularly upsetting to realize that I adopted language popularized by far-right movements whose rhetoric we should be wary of and act against.” Related Stories How Soviet TV Audiences Fell Under the Spell of Mass Hypnosis Artist Anatoly Kashpirovskiy IDFA Industry Head Says Docs Like ‘Musk’ and ‘NAZA’ Signal That Audiences Want ‘Timely’ Films: They Offer 'Something They Feel They Have to Know’ “Zio,” short for “Zionist,” has been used as a derogatory slur toward Jewish people and Israelis. Its origins trace back to Ku Klux Klan leader David Duke and white supremacists. On the Oct. 14 episode of “Las Culturistas,” Yang, his co-host Matt Rogers and guest Edy Modica were discussing Spektor, her alma mater SUNY Purchase and her music when Modica added, “And now she’s out to lunch.” Rogers asked if Modica was “upset with Regina lately,” to which she responded, “she’s just like a little Israel hardcore.” Yang added, “yeah, she’s Zio.” In recent days, social media users found the resurfaced clip of the podcast and called out Yang for using the slur. “Bowen Yang using antisemitic slang that was popularized and mainstreamed by KKK leader David Duke is really just chefs kiss for the guy who got Shane Gillis fired from ‘SNL’ for racism,” wrote Meghan McCain on X. “Well done buying this hate mongering podcast Disney.” “Las Culturistas” began streaming on Disney+ and Hulu on Wednesday. “Bowen Yang, Matt Rogers & soooo

title: Sequels, Subtitles and Spring Releases: How the Best Picture Race Is Rewriting the Academy’s Playbook
summary: The evolving Best Picture field favors sequels, international titles, and spring releases, reshaping awards strategies for actors and campaigns.
content: A preview of the best picture race with 'The Odyssey,' 'Project Hail Mary,' 'You Can See Everything' and more. Somebody at every awards season party, and everybody on the internet, will tell you why a movie can’t grab a best picture nomination — or even win the prize. It opened too early. It’s a sequel. It has subtitles. It made no money. It’s a documentary. With the fall festivals in the rearview mirror and the holiday corridor still loading, it’s time to take a look at the best picture race. Christopher Nolan’s “ The Odyssey ” holds the top spot on Variety’s best picture chart and nearly every pundit’s list. But the margin between No. 1 and No. 20 feels thinner than it has in years. Related Stories 'Searching for SmarterChild' Filmmakers Investigate Why We Insult Chatbots IDFA Head on How ‘You Can See Everything’ Phenomenon Can Pump New Blood Into Theatrical Doc Releases: ‘What Else Would This Audience See?’ A24 has many films in the projected lineup. Warner Bros., the reigning champion after its “One Battle After Another” win, with a new boss at the helm of the company, Skydance CEO David Ellison, is keeping Denis Villeneuve’s franchise finale, “ Dune: Part Three ,” close to the vest until December. And we’re still waiting for Robert Eggers’ “Werwulf,” with Aaron Taylor-Johnson. That film could shake up the race once voters finally get a look at it, and, for argument’s sake, so can “Avengers: Doomsday” from the Russo brothers. That leaves 20 to 30 films chasing 10 slots, each making its strongest case for why it belongs. Standing in the way are the old rules, and this season is poised to test every one of them. Nolan has already broken this rule himself. Universal Pictures’ “Oppenheimer” opened in July 2023 and won seven Oscars the following March. Three years later, “The Odyssey,” the adaptation of Homer’s Greek epic, has the footprint that can lead the nominations field, with an eye on the record 16 nominations “Sinners” set last season. summary: Bill Maher's comments highlight industry debates over James Bond casting identity, a factor actors must navigate in franchise roles.
content: After Grand Theft Auto VI and James Bond took over social media this week, Bill Maher has added his two cents to the discourse before going on hiatus. On Friday’s Season 24 finale of Real Time , the comedian expressed his fascination with the “giant cultural phenomenon” following GTA VI ‘s multi-billion dollar opening. “No movie ever did that,” he noted. “ Grand Theft Auto came out yesterday, and about a fifth of the young men in America stayed home and didn’t go to work, to play a game,” said Maher in his opening monologue. “This thing has caused more workplace absences than ICE.” Thursday marked the release of Grand Theft Auto VI from Rockstar Games, the first GTA installment since 2013. title: Bill Hader's Feature Directorial Debut 'They Know' Acquired by Black Bear
summary: Bill Hader's first feature, They Know, moves forward at Black Bear, signaling upcoming casting and crew opportunities.
content: Black Bear has acquired the North American rights to Bill Hader ‘s feature directorial debut “ They Know .” Hader also wrote and stars in the horror-thriller with Linda Cardellini . Based on an idea from Hader and his “Barry” collaborator Duffy Boudreau, “‘They Know’ follows a divorced dad who becomes increasingly suspicious and paranoid that his ex-wife’s new mysterious partner is exerting a strange, unsettling influence on their children,” according to an official logline. Further plot details and casting remain under wraps. Alyssa Donovan is co-producer. MRC fully financed the film, which is currently in post-production. FilmNation Entertainment is acting as the worldwide sales agent. “They Know” marks the second collaboration between Black Bear and MRC following the studio’s acquisition of “Honeymoon/Funeral,” which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival. “Bill Hader is a singular talent both in front of and behind the camera, and he has delivered a film in ‘They Know’ unlike anything we’ve ever seen,” said Michael Heimler, president of production & operations at Black Bear. “’They Know’ is authentic, original and bold filmmaking at the highest level, and we couldn’t be more excited to partner with Bill and re-team with our great friends at MRC, who consistently deliver boundary-pushing films that help define their genre.” Hader, outside of his eight-season run on “SNL,” is best known for his HBO series “Barry.” The squirmy dramedy about a contract killer with dreams of becoming an actor won 10 Emmys over its four-season run. title:
Hello Sunshine's Lauren Neustadter to Leave Reese Witherspoon's Company
 at End of Year
summary: Hello Sunshine executive Lauren Neustadter departs year-end, potentially reshaping the company's development pipeline and talent deals.
content: Lauren Neustadter , president of film and television at Reese Witherspoon ‘s Hello Sunshine , is set to step down from the company at the end of the year, the collaborators announced on Friday. Her exit comes after Hello Sunshine let go of about 50% of its staff last month after Witherspoon and Mediawan partnered to buy the company back from Candle Media. “Lauren’s taste, passion and leadership have been integral to Hello Sunshine’s film and television success,” Witherspoon said in a statement. “I’m so proud of what we accomplished together and grateful for her partnership and the lasting foundation she built around telling powerful, complex female-driven stories that resonate.” Related Stories 'Searching for SmarterChild' Filmmakers Investigate Why We Insult Chatbots 'The Year of the Ghost,' About Misogyny in China, Wins Best Film at IDFA Documentary Festival Neustadter added in a statement, “Building Hello Sunshine alongside Reese and our incredible team has been the privilege of a lifetime. I’m deeply proud of all the shows and movies we’ve made, the doors we’ve opened for new voices, and the ways we have put women in the spotlight both in front of and behind the camera. I am grateful for every moment of it, and I will always be cheering for Hello Sunshine.” Neustadter joined the company in 2017, and has served as executive producer on series including “The Morning Show,” “Big Little Lies,” “Little Fires Everywhere” and “The Last Thing He Told Me.” She oversaw adaptations of books from Reese’s Book Club including “Tiny Beautiful Things” and “Daisy Jones & the Six.” She also worked on feature films including “Where the Crawdads Sing” and TriStar’s upcoming “The Nightingale.” Neustadter started her career as a film executive at Miramax and Twentieth Century Fox, then became an executive at FOX network, where she oversaw “Brooklyn Nine-Nine,” “The Mindy Project” and “Lethal Weapon.” Hello Sunshine plans to focus on premium film and television and Reese’s Book Club,
